summary: Iteration 15 (Save whole conversation as scene) verified end-to-end. mode-header-save-thread-btn is present in the mode header BEFORE the clear (eraser) and new (plus) buttons — DOM order confirmed as ['mode-header-save-thread-btn', 'mode-header-clear-btn', 'mode-header-new-btn']. Full flow tested: login as testwriter → Collaborate mode → passage 'She stood at the edge of the garden...' → run → wait for first Jupiter reply → follow-up 'What if she never says his name aloud?' → wait for second Jupiter reply → click save-thread. window.prompt fired with suggested title 'Write with Jupiter — She stood at the edge of the garden, wai' and was accepted. A new project + scene were created; opening the scene editor confirmed the prose-editor body contains all 4 turns in correct order with '**You**' / '**Jupiter**' bold role labels separated by '\n---\n'. Counts: 2 **You**, 2 **Jupiter**, 3 '---' separators, contains original passage and follow-up prompt text. Regression: clear (Eraser) and new (Plus) buttons still function correctly after the new button was added. Empty-thread edge case: clicking save-thread with no passage/output does NOT open a prompt dialog and shows a 'Nothing to save yet' toast — verified.

issues: Since no project was active for the test user, savePassageToScene auto-creates a new project titled with the same long default (e.g., 'Write with Jupiter — She stood at the edge of the garden, wai'). This is existing behavior, not new to iter 15, but noting it — a user without an active project ends up with a new project per save-thread which may be surprising. Consider grouping into a default 'Conversations' project or reusing the last-active project.

critical_code_review_comments: saveThreadAsScene correctly uses parseTranscript and joins with role labels + '\n---\n' separators — content parsed cleanly in prose-editor.

modeLabel defaults to meta?.title ('Write with Jupiter') rather than the raw mode key ('Collaborate') as described in the request. Suggested title becomes 'Write with Jupiter — <first line>' rather than 'Collaborate — <first line>'. Behavior is fine but request wording suggests 'Collaborate — …'; consider aligning if the product owner meant the mode key.

First-line truncation at .slice(0, 40) trims mid-word (e.g., ends with 'wai'), leading to awkward titles like '... the garden, wai'. Consider trimming at the last whitespace boundary or trailing punctuation.
